answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may place jobs or claim rewards, then slash that stake when an auditable dispute proves fraud, such as taking payment without delivering. The rule does not make Sybils impossible; it makes them costly: an attacker must tie up capital in every identity and risk losing it. A hollow mesa profile gains no advantage merely by multiplying names, while copper can describe the token only if it is genuinely scarce and slashable.
